issues.legal_issue: A completed building constructed in violation of its sanctioned plan cannot be regularised through a provision permitting approval of compliant deviations during construction.
material_facts: A two-storey building plan was sanctioned, but construction proceeded to five storeys in substantial excess of the approved plan.
The municipal authority issued notices to stop the work, but construction continued.
The developer applied for regularisation after the construction had been completed.
issues.conclusion: The developer could not rely on Rule 25(2) to obtain regularisation; the application did not authorise retention of the unauthorised construction.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 25(1) of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation Building Rules, 1990 prohibits deviations from a sanctioned plan. Rule 25(2) permits a revised plan for internal alterations or external additions made during execution only where they do not violate the Act or the Rules; Rule 25(3) treats unauthorised departures as contraventions. The Court also applied the principles of planned development and strict enforcement against illegal construction discussed in Friends Colony Development Committee v. State of Orissa, Shanti Sports Club v. Union of India, and Priyanka Estates International Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Assam.

rule.if: municipal_building_enforcement_case and construction_exceeded_approved_plan and construction_completed_before_revision_application and deviation_violated_building_rules

predicates.municipal_building_enforcement_case: The proceeding concerned enforcement of municipal controls over building construction.
predicates.construction_exceeded_approved_plan: The person responsible constructed a building beyond the plan approved by the municipal authority.
predicates.construction_completed_before_revision_a: The person responsible applied for approval of a revised plan after completing the disputed construction.
predicates.deviation_violated_building_rules: The deviation from the approved plan contravened the applicable building requirements.

issues.definition: When a municipal building-enforcement proceeding concerns completed construction that exceeds the approved plan and violates building requirements, the deviation procedure cannot be used to regularise it.

issues.legal_issue: A direction to reconsider demolition is unsustainable when the competent municipal authority has already ordered demolition and the unauthorised construction is admitted.
material_facts: The municipal authority issued notices concerning the unauthorised construction and the developer continued building despite a stop-work notice.
The Mayor-in-Council had resolved that the unauthorised construction be demolished, and part of it was demolished.
The developer admitted that the building had been constructed contrary to the sanctioned plan.
The High Court Division Bench directed the municipal authority to make a fresh decision on retention or demolition without accounting for the existing demolition decision.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the Division Bench’s direction for a fresh decision because the competent authority had already ordered demolition and the unauthorised construction was undisputed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 400, 401 and 401A of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation Act, 1980, the municipal authorities may take action against unauthorised construction, including demolition. The Court held that the High Court’s direction could not stand where the record showed that the competent authority had already decided to demolish the construction. Its approach was consistent with the enforcement of building controls affirmed in Friends Colony Development Committee v. State of Orissa and Priyanka Estates International Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Assam.

predicates.appeal_from_demolition_order: The proceeding was an appeal concerning an order for demolition of unauthorised construction.
predicates.authority_had_already_ordered_demolition: The competent municipal authority had decided that the unauthorised construction should be demolished.
predicates.unauthorized_construction_admitted: The person responsible acknowledged that the construction departed from the sanctioned plan.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning demolition, a fresh decision is unwarranted when the competent authority has already ordered demolition and the unauthorised nature of the construction is admitted.

issues.legal_issue: A developer who raises unauthorised construction and sells portions of it to purchasers must compensate those purchasers and bear a penalty for the violation.
material_facts: The developer constructed a five-storey building when only a two-storey building had been sanctioned and continued construction despite a stop-work notice.
The developer sold portions of the unauthorised building to purchasers who believed it had been constructed in accordance with the sanctioned plan.
Demolition of the unauthorised portions would leave some purchasers without shelter.
The unauthorised construction burdened public amenities and was found to pose safety and other public risks.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed the developer to refund the purchasers’ payments with interest and to pay a monetary cost for the brazen violation of the sanctioned plan and continued construction despite the stop-work notice.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle that illegal construction harms planned development, public amenities and safety, and that purchasers who are victims of a builder’s unauthorised construction should be compensated. It relied on the observations in Friends Colony Development Committee v. State of Orissa concerning compensation for unwary purchasers, and in Pratibha Coop. Housing Society Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra and Priyanka Estates International Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Assam concerning the need for firm action against unauthorised construction.

rule.if: municipal_building_enforcement_case and developer_built_without_plan_compliance and developer_sold_unauthorized_units_to_bona_fide_purchasers and demolition_will_displace_purchasers

predicates.municipal_building_enforcement_case: The proceeding concerned enforcement against unauthorised building construction.
predicates.developer_built_without_plan_compliance: The developer constructed the building in violation of the approved plan.
predicates.developer_sold_unauthorized_units_to_bon: The developer sold portions of the unauthorised building to purchasers who believed the construction complied with the approved plan.
predicates.demolition_will_displace_purchasers: Demolition of the unauthorised portions would deprive purchasers of their occupied homes.

issues.definition: When a developer violates the approved plan, sells unauthorised units to purchasers acting in good faith, and demolition will displace them, the developer must compensate those purchasers and bear a penalty.
